page: Amazon Web Services r6g.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The underlying virtualization is managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate balanced multi-core and memory performance, though single-core execution speeds represent a notable tradeoff. The server achieves average tier results in multi-core processing, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48584.84 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11647.0. Memory bandwidth is robust, measuring 1893.45 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 165.0 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-threaded performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0 and lower-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression and text processing. Large-language model inference speeds also fall into the lower performance tier, particularly for prompt processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r6g.8xlarge leverages the ARM64 architecture to deliver high memory density and dedicated physical cores without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from parallel physical cores rather than raw single-thread speed. Appropriate workloads include in-memory databases like Redis, which achieved 37.16 million operations per second in testing, as well as distributed caching, database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks.
